knowledge_gaps: Averaging recent SASRec hidden states does not isolate recent interactions: each state already summarizes its causal prefix. The report needs evidence that this readout strengthens recent intent rather than smoothing contextual representations. Compare the unchanged baseline, fixed-gate pooling, and learned-gate pooling under matched training settings.

Training-suffix targets have already influenced model fitting, so their diagnostic HR@10 measures training behavior rather than generalization. Deleting interactions also changes sequence length, absolute positions, and truncation. These effects require explicit controls before interpreting recent-versus-older deletion differences.

Reproduction details remain incomplete: probe user counts, suffix selection, deletion sizes, candidate construction, tie handling, gate initialization and monitoring, checkpoint selection, and GPU-budget allocation are unspecified. Top-10 overlap over sampled candidates must be distinguished from full-catalog overlap.

The potential and difficulty scores are provisional. A global scalar gate cannot adapt to different user contexts or measure compatibility, redundancy, or immediate intent. Implementation difficulty also includes efficient differentiable pooling, causal and padding checks, and numerical agreement between training and the generated predictor.

follow_up_queries.reason: Assess the architectural rationale and identify simple controls that distinguish recency benefits from generic smoothing.
